items.title: ‘Eastside Festival’ 2027 lineup brings Mesh, Kite and Heppner’s TanzZwang to Halle
items.summary: Eastside Festival returns to Karlsbad, Halle (Saale) on 2-3 July 2027 with Mesh, Kite, Heppner's TanzZwang, TRAITRS, Ductape and Then Comes Silence.
items.fullText:
Eastside Festival returns to Halle (Saale), Germany, on 2-3 July 2027, bringing two days of synthpop, EBM, darkwave, post-punk and alternative electronic music to the lakeside setting of Karlsbad at Angersdorfer Teiche. Now entering its fifth year, the festival has announced a lineup combining established names with newer projects, including Mesh, Kite, Heppner’s TanzZwang, TRAITRS, Ductape, Then Comes Silence, T.O.Y., DSTR, The Sound Veil Society and Unify Separate.

Organised by Hamburg-based PLUSWELT PROMOTION in cooperation with Karlsbad and Freizeit und Event GmbH, and presented alongside Sonic Seducer, Eastside Festival originated as an idea during the pandemic. Since then, it has developed into a regular meeting point for audiences interested in alternative electronic music, favouring a relatively intimate atmosphere over the scale of larger European festivals. Its unusual location, with a sandy beach, lakeside views and camping facilities, provides a rather different environment for a programme devoted to darker sounds.

Eastside Festival 2027 headliners: Mesh and Kite

Among the leading names for 2027 are Mesh, the British electronic duo whose combination of melodic synthpop, sophisticated production and emotionally direct songwriting has earned them a longstanding international following. Their appearance follows the release of “The Truth Doesn’t Matter” in March 2026, their first studio album in nearly a decade. The record addresses contemporary uncertainty, fractured relationships and the uneasy relationship between truth and perception, extending the band’s familiar musical vocabulary into a new period of creative activity.

Swedish duo Kite, consisting of Nicklas Stenemo and Christian Berg, will also headline the festival. Their music combines dramatic synthesizer arrangements, expansive melodies and an often theatrical approach to live presentation. Their 2024 release “VII,” gathering material from the duo’s series of singles, demonstrated the breadth of their electronic songwriting, including collaborations with Blanck Mass, Anna von Hausswolff and Henric de la Cour. Kite’s concerts have become known for their elaborate visual production, making their appearance an interesting addition to Eastside’s outdoor setting.

Heppner’s TanzZwang, TRAITRS and more join the bill

Another notable booking is Heppner’s TanzZwang, the electronic live project associated with Peter Heppner, whose unmistakable voice has played an important role in German synthpop since his years with Wolfsheim. TanzZwang places greater emphasis on dance-oriented electronic arrangements, moving Heppner’s distinctive vocal style into a more direct club environment.

The darker, guitar-driven side of the programme is represented by TRAITRS, the Canadian post-punk duo whose austere arrangements, insistent rhythms and emotionally charged vocals draw upon the traditions of gothic rock and darkwave. Their music combines an unmistakable connection to earlier post-punk with contemporary production, making them a natural fit for the festival’s broader aesthetic.

Ductape, the Turkish duo formed by Çağla and Furkan Güleray, bring another perspective on contemporary darkwave. Having developed their sound through extensive international touring, they released their fourth album, “Faded Flowers,” in September 2026. Their combination of driving basslines, guitar, synthesizers and expressive vocals has become increasingly distinctive, with the new material exploring alienation, emotional distance and the contradictions of contemporary life.

Sweden’s Then Comes Silence are another important name for post-punk and gothic rock audiences. Led by Alex Svenson, the group have developed a recognisable sound built around bass-driven arrangements, sharp guitar lines and a strong melodic sensibility. Their eighth studio album, “Requiem Ballroom,” released in November 2026 through Metropolis Records, provides fresh material for a band whose live performances retain a direct connection to gothic rock’s darker, more physical traditions.

The electronic selection extends further with DSTR, the project of Daniel Myer, whose extensive work with Haujobb, Architect and numerous other collaborations has made him one of the most active figures in contemporary electro-industrial music. DSTR offers a more melodic and dance-oriented outlet for his production interests, retaining the detailed electronic construction associated with his other projects while approaching songwriting from a different perspective.

T.O.Y. add another established name from the German electronic scene, while Unify Separate bring their combination of synthesizer-driven songwriting and expansive alternative influences to the programme. Their third album, “The God Particle,” released in November 2026, further develops the partnership between Andrew Montgomery and Leo Josefsson, balancing melodic accessibility with a more substantial electronic sound.

Another act worth noting is The Sound Veil Society, the Swedish-Norwegian duo of Erlend Eilertsen and Hans-Olof Mattsson. Their debut album, “Things We Kept,” released through Progress Productions in September 2026, introduced a project concerned with detailed electronic arrangements and atmospheric songwriting. Their inclusion reflects Eastside’s interest in presenting newer artists alongside musicians with considerably longer histories.

The lineup also features KY and M/A/T, the latter founded by Matthias Bischoff, formerly of the synthpop and EBM project Cyber. M/A/T’s music draws upon the rhythmic traditions of classic electronic body music, synthpop and dark disco, bringing another dancefloor-oriented element to the festival.

Special performances at Eastside Festival 2027

Beyond the main concerts, Eastside will offer several additional performances designed for the more informal lakeside environment. Elektro All-Stars will present their EBM karaoke concept, already familiar to visitors of the Wave-Gotik-Treffen warm-up events. Vaughn George will perform his interpretations of Depeche Mode songs by the lake, while Kyle Blaqk of Auger is scheduled for a special acoustic set in the same setting.

These smaller performances are an important part of the festival’s character. Instead of concentrating exclusively on the main stage, Eastside makes use of its location to provide opportunities for audiences to experience music in a more relaxed atmosphere, away from the intensity of conventional concert venues.

The Karlsbad site at Angersdorfer Teiche offers a spacious sandy beach, camping facilities and the opportunity to spend the weekend beside the water. For visitors accustomed to experiencing dark electronic music in crowded clubs, former industrial buildings and enclosed festival halls, the combination of open-air concerts, summer evenings and lakeside surroundings provides an appealing change of scenery.

The organisers emphasise that Eastside was conceived primarily as a gathering for audiences interested in alternative music, not as a commercially driven mainstream event. Its programming reflects that approach, bringing together international artists, established scene favourites and newer names whose work spans different branches of electronic and guitar-based alternative music.

With Mesh and Kite leading the bill, Heppner’s TanzZwang adding a club-oriented dimension, and artists such as TRAITRS, Ductape, Then Comes Silence and DSTR broadening the musical selection, Eastside 2027 offers a well-balanced programme for followers of synthpop, EBM, darkwave and post-punk. Its lakeside setting remains one of its most distinctive features, offering a weekend where the music may be dark, but the surroundings are decidedly summery. This is the fifth edition of the festival, following Eastside Festival 2026, which brought Nitzer Ebb, Covenant and Devision Redux to the same site.

Eastside Festival 2027: dates, lineup and tickets

  • Dates: Friday 2 July – Saturday 3 July 2027
  • Venue: Karlsbad, Angersdorfer Teiche 9, 06126 Halle (Saale), Germany
  • Confirmed lineup: Mesh, Kite, Heppner’s TanzZwang, TRAITRS, Ductape, Then Comes Silence, T.O.Y., DSTR, The Sound Veil Society, Unify Separate, KY and M/A/T
  • Special performances: Elektro All-Stars (EBM karaoke), Vaughn George (Depeche Mode interpretations by the lake), Kyle Blaqk of Auger (lakeside acoustic set)
  • Organisers: PLUSWELT PROMOTION, Karlsbad and Freizeit und Event GmbH, with Sonic Seducer as presenting partner

Weekend tickets are available as original printed tickets or print-at-home tickets through the official ticket shop. Separate camping options are also available, subject to availability. More information is on the festival website and the venue’s own site.

items.title: Xotox – ‘Wir hatten doch Träume’ (Digital Single – Infacted Recordings)
items.summary: Xotox releases 'Wir hatten doch Träume', a three-track digital single via Infacted Recordings, out 2 October 2026.
items.fullText:
German industrial electronic project Xotox, led by Andreas Davids, released “Wir hatten doch Träume” (“We Used to Have Dreams”) on 2 October 2026 through Infacted Recordings. The three-track digital single explores the uncertain afterlife of shared dreams, the gradual erosion of emotional intimacy and the realisation that moments once tied to happiness may now exist only in memory.

The title suggests an unfinished conversation, recalling promises and aspirations whose meaning has shifted with time. The accompanying release notes describe dreams and longings overwhelmed by “emotional noise,” fading into pale grey. For an artist whose musical identity has long been tied to rhythmic noise, the phrase carries added resonance. Mechanical repetition and electronic force surround something more vulnerable here: the persistence of memories that refuse to disappear even as their emotional weight becomes harder to grasp.

The title track draws on the experience of a specific night that unexpectedly surfaces forgotten dreams and emotions, only for them to slip away again. Xotox treats that nostalgia as something less reassuring than a comforting return to the past, and confronts the distance between what people once imagined their lives might become and what remains of those expectations.

Musically, the release brings Davids’ established interest in forceful electronic rhythms into contact with a more pronounced melodic sensibility. The contrast between the precision of programmed structures and the uncertainty of the subject matter gives the title track an expressive character beyond the physical intensity usually associated with rhythmic noise: the electronics keep their mechanical discipline while the melodic elements add a quieter sense of longing.

The single also includes “Cherophobia” and “Hypnose.” The latter runs past seven minutes, more than half of the release’s total length.

“Wir hatten doch Träume” was recorded by Xotox at Separate Room, MTH, in 2026, with mastering by Anatoly Grinberg.

Tracklist: – Wir hatten doch Träume – 3:30 – Cherophobia – 3:19 – Hypnose – 7:17

“Wir hatten doch Träume” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

About Xotox

Founded in Germany in 1998 by Andreas Davids, Xotox released several self-published albums between 1998 and 2002 before signing to Pronoize. Its 2003 album “Lichtlos” became the first album by an industrial act to reach number one on the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The track “[PSI]” reached number two on the same chart in 2005, and 2008’s “In den zehn Morgen” spent six weeks at number one. The project built its catalogue around distorted electronic rhythms, aggressive percussion and atmospheric synthesizers, including the compilation “Essentials (Best Of)” in 2016.

Since joining Infacted Recordings in 2019, Xotox has continued to develop its sound through releases including the 2023 album “Ich bin da / Ich funtioniere”, the 2025 album “Particles” and the remix collection “Dokumentation II: Remix” in 2026. Davids discussed the project’s fusion of techno and industrial elements in a 2020 “Click Interview” with Side-Line. “Wir hatten doch Träume” extends that catalogue with a more melodic turn across its three new tracks.

items.title: Robert J Revell interview: ‘Creation is the point’
items.summary: Robert J Revell talks to Side-Line about The SPKtR's European tour, his solo album "Torn Remnants of Nobility" and working with father Graeme Revell.
items.fullText:
There is something almost paradoxical about Robert J Revell. Onstage, he is an extraordinary physical presence, throwing himself into performances with an intensity that can be exhilarating, unsettling and occasionally difficult to watch. Away from the stage, however, he speaks with remarkable openness about humility, family, artistic responsibility and the complicated relationship between creativity and self-worth.

At the 25th anniversary edition of Wrocław Industrial Festival, Karo Kratochwil experienced both sides of his musical work. His solo performance, drawing upon the visceral, psychologically charged material of “Torn Remnants of Nobility”, revealed an artist whose relationship with sound is intensely physical and deeply personal. The following evening, performing alongside his father, industrial music pioneer Graeme Revell, in The SPKtR, he brought that same instinctive energy into a very different creative environment.

The contrast was revealing. Where Graeme approaches composition through carefully developed structures and technological experimentation, Robert introduces an element of unpredictability, allowing the performance to develop through spontaneous physical responses to sound. Their collaboration is built around those differences, bringing two generations and contrasting artistic philosophies into direct contact.

Yet Robert’s interests extend far beyond industrial music. A multi-instrumentalist with a background spanning death metal, thrash, noise, experimental electronics and numerous other genres, he has created an extensive catalogue of largely unreleased recordings. He also builds and dismantles theatre sets, using the same processes of welding, machinery and manual labour that seem strangely appropriate to his musical world.

During the conversation, Robert reflects on the realities of touring, the unexpected responses to his performances, his relationship with Graeme, the emotional foundations of his solo work and the importance of creating without becoming attached to the result.

Robert J Revell interview

Karo: Robert, I had the pleasure of seeing both your solo performance and The SPKtR at Wrocław Industrial Festival. Two very different experiences, both extraordinarily intense. Looking back, what surprised you most about those two nights?

Robert: For a genre where audiences are accustomed to watching a person stand over a table, tweaking a laptop or a mixer, I was surprised to get the feedback “more vocals, less computer”. It’s interesting to me in that I thought “singing” to the audience might come across as rockstar shit. Not very “industrial”. But it makes sense that we all want connection regardless of the context. I’ve been welcomed into this community and I’m very grateful for it, so I try to approach situations with humility. In most areas of my life, but especially here. I’m glad for the feedback because it aligns with my interests for live performance.

Karo: Wrocław also marked the beginning of your European tour with The SPKtR. How has the journey been unfolding so far? Has anything happened onstage that neither you nor Graeme expected?

Robert: When I first heard the tracks live through a PA, it was at WIF. Previously I’d listened to them on my home stereo, which is pretty powerful but nothing by comparison. So when the show started I immediately became energized and viscerally inspired. And that keeps happening every night. That’s how I end up bashing my hands on the cage, or hanging from the lighting rig, or beating the floor with the metal rods. Every night is a surprise for me. I don’t know what I’ll end up doing.

Karo: Touring takes you through so many cities, people and fleeting encounters. When the venues and setlists begin to blur together, what actually stays with you?

Robert: The way the peaks of the waves light up while I look out the porthole of the night ferry. The way the sun plays hide and seek behind the clouds but you don’t know if it’ll come back at all that day. The excited and hopefully inspired faces of the people I’ve gotten to meet. The way it’s only been a couple weeks but my kids look more grown up already.

Karo: Your biography mentions nearly twenty unreleased albums spanning different genres. What made “Torn Remnants of Nobility” the first one you wanted the world to hear? And is there something liberating about creating music without knowing whether anyone will ever listen to it?

Robert: Art should be made with no consideration of its reception. Then it’s pure. One can choose to edit later if deemed necessary. It’s paramount to be genuine and sincere. People can tell right away if you’re not.

The reason I released Torn Remnants was because I was asked. After the 2025 shows in Pordenone and the VOD Fest I was contacted by a few people about a possible release. So I made an album and sent it off. Walter from Klanggalerie was the most excited about it so I went with him. He’s such a genuine music lover and truly kind person, it’s infectious.

I tend to be quite nihilistic about almost everything in life except the people I love and who love me. So “releasing” music never really occurred to me. Who am I to believe “the world needs to hear this”? I make music for myself and that’s enough.

Karo: The album explores violence, shame, regret and some profoundly uncomfortable aspects of human experience. Does transforming these emotions into music change your relationship with them, or is the act of expression itself what matters?

Robert: The act of releasing these emotions in a live setting is what’s important. It’s catharsis. To be honest in front of people where there’s nowhere to hide is irreplaceable. And if it speaks to someone who might feel the same way but may not be able to put it into words then that’s great. I’ve been on the other side of that so many times in my life as an audience member that it’s only fair to attempt to return the favor.

I’ve also released a “game” called Transient Rumination Original Nascence. It’s an answer to the negative vomit of Torn Remnants. So the themes of Torn Remnants have an answer in Transient Rumination. Things that have helped me to deal with those “negative” emotions. It also has a process to write a poem in a few minutes.

I find that when I’ve completed a task, or especially a piece of art, then I can sort of justify breathing the air, and taking up some precious resources as a guest on this planet Earth.

Karo: “Forgiveness in the Face of Regret” closes the album. Forgiveness isn’t necessarily the end of an emotional struggle. What does it mean to you in the context of this record?

Robert: Forgiveness is a battle. In this case it’s forgiveness of self. No one hates like the self. We are the pigs in the slaughterhouse covered in shit, consuming and consuming. The shame and guilt of that begs forgiveness.

Karo: You’ve played everything from death metal and thrash to experimental electronics and noise. Have you ever encountered an emotion or an idea that one musical language simply couldn’t express, forcing you to find another?

Robert: Not yet. But I do tend to keep the musical languages separate. I try to express the emotions at one time, working on one project with one language. Torn Remnants is the most eclectic thing I’ve done. But the genre allows for that in my opinion.

Karo: You also work in theatre construction, building sets from metal and wood, welding and working with heavy machinery. Has that experience changed the way you understand sound?

Robert: I’ve always loved machines and processes. I started with stereo equipment, moved to rebuilding old cars and motorcycles. That’s where the welding came in.

Everything I enjoy is bad for my ears. Building loud engines with no mufflers, fixing and riding motorcycles, playing in bands, going to concerts, building structures and roofing using nail guns and saws.

I attempt to protect my hearing when I can but I enjoy the feeling. So the sounds of machines satisfy a part of me that “music” does. They are one and the same.

Karo: Theatre sets can require enormous amounts of work, only to be dismantled when a production ends. Does knowing that something you’ve created is temporary affect your attachment to it?

Robert: When the show is over, some parts of the set are salvaged and the rest is destroyed and disposed of. That’s my favorite part. To destroy something you’ve created like the Tibetan Buddhist monks and the Dissolution Ceremony is a display of intense appreciation for beauty while almost simultaneously recognizing its temporary nature.

Except rather than brushing away sand I use a sledgehammer.

It’s reflected in how I sign my CD or book. The painting I created for Torn Remnants or the photo I took for Blurred Recollections and Suspended Moments gets covered in Sharpie in a haphazard way to remind myself not to be precious or egotistical about my work.

Karo: When we spoke at Wrocław Industrial Festival, you mentioned that both your parents had always supported your artistic endeavours. Was there a particular moment when their encouragement gave you the confidence to pursue something unconventional?

Robert: I think it’s been constant. My Mum would constantly prepare art projects for us. And I see it with her and my kids. She always has a fun engaging way to teach people that they can do anything. Anything in the world. The confidence she inspires is staggering.

Karo: You were only ten when you discovered “Information Overload Unit” and realised that your father had created music that seemed to reflect what was happening inside your own mind. Did that discovery change your understanding of what music could actually do?

Robert: When I first heard it I just got really excited. Yes yes yes!!! This is it!! I love this!!!! Then weeks later I found out it was him. So when people tell me they’ve been a fan of SPK for decades, I say me too! What an honor it is to be a part of The SPKtR and to play some of the old songs.

Karo: You’ve known Graeme your entire life, but working with someone creatively can reveal unexpected sides of their personality. What’s something you’ve discovered about your father through making music together that you might never have learned otherwise?

Robert: We are extremely similar in so many ways. Mostly in personality. Our approach musically is very different.

He’s always been excited about new possibilities that emerging technology allows. Looking back over his career it’s incredibly obvious to anyone that the sounds he envisioned were right on the cusp of availability. His voice speaks for the future of humanity. A future that hasn’t happened yet but is definitely coming.

On the other hand, my work is deeply personal and in the moment. My performances are the same way. For me the future does not exist and the past is just a memory skewed by my own recollection. Now is all we have.

Karo: Graeme has described you as The SPKtR’s improvisational wildcard. When you’re onstage together, how do you recognise the moment when a composition needs to be challenged rather than followed?

Robert: He has a specific vision for everything. He’s extremely calculated and focused on the details. This is perfect for me.

While I am a detail-oriented person I much prefer to let my instincts take over. i.e. building a set to exact measurements and specifications is satisfying, but destroying it by kicking down walls, tearing pieces off or smashing through materials is much more fun.

After our very first performance together in Pordenone, he saw that in me, and saw that I was very comfortable on stage. He then got me an axe and an oil drum and a pig’s head for the VOD Fest. Then I felt like the Tasmanian Devil just waiting for the signal.

Karo: Your performances can be almost frightening in their intensity, yet there’s also something playful about your approach to extremes. Do you ever find yourself having an enormous amount of fun while the audience is experiencing something almost terrifying?

Robert: I’m always having a great time. The extreme expression is very comfortable for me.

There was a moment at WIF where there was a disagreement in the front row between a man and a woman. I was thrashing around and yelling but as soon as I saw a man yelling at a woman I was present and tried my best to escalate the situation.

The people I know that experience extreme emotions are comfortable there and have a lifetime of practice in controlling them.

Karo: Between your own recordings, The SPKtR, theatre and all the different forms of music you’ve explored, you’ve already created an extraordinary amount of work. Is there something you still haven’t made that you would genuinely regret leaving unrealised?

Robert: I love and appreciate this question. There are artists whose responses I’d love to hear. For me however, it requires ego that I’ve tried very hard to rid myself of.

Also, the distance between ideation and creation is very short for me, in terms of timeline. Creation starts in planning so that the execution is streamlined.

If I can empty my cup of a need to create, by creating as often as possible then my desires are revealed to be ego feeding. Creation is the point.

Whether it’s “good enough” upon listening back is an attempt at measuring oneself against what we think we should be. Maybe one day when I’m perfect, I’ll care.

Karo: The Wrocław performance provoked some strong reactions, including criticism that became quite personal. How do you respond when judgments about the music turn into judgments about the people making it?

Robert: There are things in my life that are so fundamentally important. Things I would die for. Things I would kill for. Things for which I would suffer a thousand slow deaths. Things I would do unspeakable evils to protect. And they are people. My Wife, my Children, my Family, my Loved ones. Anyone who knows me, knows that I mean every word of this, and I am more than capable of executing it with excruciating longevity.

By comparison, everything else falls so far short. The uninformed opinion of a stranger? Laughable.

I’ve seen people posting a sentiment over the years that “Industrial used to be dangerous” and “artists used to take risks”. That’s exactly what The SPKtR is doing in every way. Nothing is the same old shit. Everything is a new creation and some of it is rocky to coordinate.

If people have a problem with that then great. Not one of those people has offered a suggestion of what would be a better performance. Just complaints.

There are very few people around today who were actually at the old SPK shows and there’s a romanticized version in their heads of everything being so perfect and that everyone loved it. I’ve been told by someone who was at every single SPK gig that that’s not the case.

So when people have a reaction to The SPKtR it’s actually closer to the reactions that they got all those years ago. Some love, some hate, some appreciation and some disgust. My Dad has literal scars to prove it.

So while the material has changed in 40 years, the experience is actually closer to what it was.

About Robert J. Revell

Robert J. Revell is an Australian-born musician, composer and multidisciplinary artist from Sydney, currently based in Los Angeles. His work encompasses industrial music, experimental electronics, noise, musique concrète, metal, sound composition and performance art.

A multi-instrumentalist with experience as a guitarist, vocalist, bassist and drummer, Revell has performed and recorded across numerous genres, including death metal, thrash, doom, jazz, blues and experimental music. Alongside his musical activities, he builds theatre sets, combining carpentry, welding and mechanical engineering skills with an interest in physical structures and the processes of creation and destruction.

His debut solo album, “Torn Remnants of Nobility”, was released by Austrian experimental label Klanggalerie on 8 November 2025. The six-track recording explores difficult psychological territory through abrasive electronics, extreme instrumental textures and compositions concerned with violence, shame, guilt, regret and the possibility of emotional release. Revell wrote, recorded, mixed and created the artwork for the album himself.

Despite maintaining an extensive archive of approximately twenty largely unreleased albums, as well as music for film, television and theatre, Revell has generally approached composition as a personal necessity rather than a means of pursuing commercial recognition.

He is also a member of The SPKtR, the contemporary incarnation of SPK, the first-wave industrial project founded by his father, Graeme Revell. Their collaboration brings together Graeme’s compositional and technological approach with Robert’s instinctive, physically demanding performance style. In 2025, father and son appeared together in Pordenone, Italy, and at the Vinyl-on-Demand Festival. Their collaboration subsequently developed into the extensive European tour undertaken in November and December 2026, including their appearance at the 25th anniversary of Wrocław Industrial Festival.

More on Robert J. Revell’s music: klanggalerie.bandcamp.com/album/torn-remnants-of-nobility, linktr.ee/robertjrevell. More on The SPKtR: thespktr.org.

items.title: Happy birthday, Chris Watson, co-founder of Cabaret Voltaire
items.summary: Chris Watson, co-founder of Cabaret Voltaire, turns 73 on 21 November 2026. A look at his industrial music years and his field recording career since.
items.fullText:
Chris Watson, co-founder of Sheffield industrial group Cabaret Voltaire, turns 73 on 21 November 2026. Watson helped shape the band’s early, abrasive sound before leaving in 1981 to build an internationally recognised career in field recording and wildlife sound, work that has since earned him three BAFTA awards for Best Factual Sound.

Today we celebrate Chris Watson, one of the founding figures of British industrial music and an artist whose career has taken him from the experimental electronic underground of Sheffield to some of the most remote acoustic environments on Earth.

In 1973, Watson co-founded Cabaret Voltaire with Richard H. Kirk and Stephen Mallinder. Using tape loops, found sounds, primitive electronics and manipulated recordings, the trio challenged conventional ideas of composition, rhythm and instrumentation and developed an abrasive, often unsettling language that became fundamental to the emergence of industrial music. Early releases such as “Mix-Up” (1979), “The Voice of America” (1980) and “Red Mecca” (1981) remain key documents of a period when electronic experimentation was becoming inseparable from the political and cultural tensions of post-industrial Britain.

After leaving Cabaret Voltaire in 1981, Watson joined Tyne Tees Television and continued his sound experiments through The Hafler Trio, formed with Andrew M. McKenzie, before developing an extraordinary career in wildlife and environmental recording. His subsequent work for television, radio and documentary productions, including BBC natural history programmes with Sir David Attenborough, allowed him to pursue an interest that had been present since his earliest experiments with tape: the possibility of discovering musical structures within sounds that already exist around us. That work has brought him three BAFTA awards for Best Factual Sound, for “The Life of Birds” (1998), “Frozen Planet” (2012) and “The Secret World of Sound with David Attenborough” (2025).

His solo recordings, including “Stepping into the Dark” (1996), “Weather Report” (2003) and “El Tren Fantasma” (2011), demonstrate an exceptional sensitivity to acoustic detail, duration and the spatial character of sound. From the movement of glaciers and the calls of wildlife to the mechanical rhythms of a train crossing Mexico, Watson builds sonic narratives from these recordings without relying on conventional musical instrumentation. Careful editing and composition give these recordings relationships between sounds that a casual listen would miss.

2026 has been another busy year in Watson’s career. Following Cabaret Voltaire’s 50th-anniversary return to the stage in 2025, he and Stephen Mallinder embarked on farewell performances celebrating the group’s legacy and their late collaborator Richard H. Kirk, who died in 2021. Watson also released “Planet Ocean” through Touch, an album of recordings devoted to the rhythms, textures and acoustic life of the world’s oceans.

Watson’s artistic journey ties these different worlds together. The musician who once experimented with tape manipulation and electronic noise in Sheffield has spent decades investigating the equally complex sonic structures of nature, applying the same curiosity and attention to sounds that conventional listening frequently overlooks.

Happy birthday, Chris Watson. Thank you for an extraordinary contribution to industrial and experimental music, for the pioneering work of Cabaret Voltaire, and for decades of recordings that have expanded what sound, and listening itself, can reveal.

About Chris Watson

Chris Watson was born on 21 November 1953 in the Sheffield suburb of Totley, England. He is a musician, sound artist and field recordist whose career spans both experimental electronic music and contemporary sound art. In 1973 he co-founded the pioneering industrial group Cabaret Voltaire alongside Richard H. Kirk and Stephen Mallinder. His early experiments with tape manipulation, found sounds and electronics on albums including “Mix-Up”, “The Voice of America” and “Red Mecca” contributed to a musical language that went on to influence generations of industrial, post-punk and electronic artists.

Following his departure from Cabaret Voltaire in October 1981, Watson joined Tyne Tees Television and formed The Hafler Trio with Andrew M. McKenzie before establishing himself as one of the world’s leading specialists in wildlife and environmental sound recording. His work has taken him across the globe, capturing the acoustic environments of remote landscapes, animal habitats and natural phenomena, and he has contributed to BBC natural history productions associated with Sir David Attenborough, including “The Life of Birds”, “Frozen Planet” and “The Secret World of Sound with David Attenborough”, which brought him BAFTA awards for Best Factual Sound in 1998, 2012 and 2025 respectively.

His solo releases on the Touch label include “Stepping into the Dark” (1996), “Outside the Circle of Fire” (1998), “Weather Report” (2003, named one of “1000 albums to hear before you die” by The Guardian in 2007), “El Tren Fantasma” (2011) and “Planet Ocean” (2026). Through these recordings, Watson transforms environmental sound into acoustic works that sit between music, documentary and sound art.

In May 2025, Watson and Mallinder announced they would reunite as Cabaret Voltaire for a 50th-anniversary performance at Sheffield’s Sensoria Festival, followed by a final tour and the live album “But What Time Is It Really?” through 2026, alongside an ongoing reissue campaign for “CODE” on Mute. Official website: chriswatson.net.

items.title: Toy Weather’s 1995 album ‘Seasons Of Fairytales’ gets a digital reissue via Sub Culture Records
items.summary: Toy Weather's 1995 album "Seasons Of Fairytales" is now a digital reissue via Sub Culture Records on Bandcamp, released November 20, 2026.
items.fullText:
More than three decades after its original release, Norwegian electronic project Toy Weather’s album Seasons Of Fairytales is getting another chance to be discovered. Sub Culture Records released the 14-track album digitally on November 20, 2026.

Originally released on CD in 1995, “Seasons Of Fairytales” was written and produced by Svein Hovland. The album draws on several musical styles, with elements of electronic music, art rock, progressive rock and darker, more experimental sounds.

The record moves between different musical approaches without sticking to one particular genre, reflecting a time when electronic music was exploring territory well beyond the dancefloor.

The album includes tracks such as “The Season Of Fairytales”, “Moods Like Jeans”, “The Better Of Mysteries”, “Shadow Pictures” and “Quiet On The Western Front”.

With this digital reissue, Sub Culture Records is bringing a piece of Norwegian electronic music history back into circulation. For those who remember the original CD, it is an opportunity to hear the album again. For everyone else, it is a chance to discover a recording that first appeared more than 30 years ago.

  8. Do Or Die
  9. Kill My Dreams

About Toy Weather

Toy Weather is the recording project of Norwegian musician Svein Hovland. “Seasons Of Fairytales” first appeared on CD in 1995, before streaming and digital distribution gave older recordings this kind of second life.

Hovland kept releasing music as Toy Weather in the years since. In 2026, the project returned with the album “Feathers in a Strange Wind” on Apollon Records, with Hovland on vocals and guitar alongside Frank Hovland on bass and Rune Kogstad on drums, and a standalone single, “Woodstock Morning”. The reissue of “Seasons Of Fairytales” through Sub Culture Records gives listeners a way to hear where that sound started, three decades earlier.

items.title: Fear Maintenance releases ‘New Dawn Fades’ cover and video
items.summary: Solo project Fear Maintenance released a cover of Joy Division's "New Dawn Fades" with a self-made video on November 18, 2026, its third post-punk single.
items.fullText:
Burlington, Ontario solo project Fear Maintenance released a cover of Joy Division’s “New Dawn Fades” on November 18, 2026, its third single since musician Colin Adams began reworking post-punk songs under the name. The track is also available on Spotify and other streaming services.

Adams arranged, performed, produced, recorded, mixed and mastered the cover alone in his Burlington home studio over four months. He built the arrangement around the final minute of Joy Division’s original, extending the instrumental coda that follows Ian Curtis’s last line into what Adams calls a “sonic explosion,” describing it as the sound of someone in the middle of an emotional breakdown.

Adams also conceived, shot and edited the video himself, working with a green screen in a ten-by-eight-foot space in his basement over four months, usually shooting between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. He describes the approach as reflecting “the internal strife and self-loathing of the protagonist as he metaphorically beat himself up.”

“New Dawn Fades” is track five on Joy Division’s debut album “Unknown Pleasures,” released by Factory Records in June 1979 following sessions with producer Martin Hannett at Strawberry Studios in Stockport. An instrumental edit of a Moby cover of the song appeared in Michael Mann’s 1995 film “Heat.”

About Fear Maintenance

Fear Maintenance is the solo project of Colin Adams, a musician based in Burlington, Ontario, Canada, who plays, produces and records all of its material alone in his home studio. The project revisits post-punk songs from the late 1970s and 1980s that Adams says inspired him to become a musician, and has released no original material under the name.

Adams was fifteen when he joined the Toronto band Face of Another as guitarist in 1986. Its bassist, Tim Smith, introduced him to Joy Division; the two later fell out and never spoke again. After Smith’s death, Adams and his former bandmates revisited their old songs for Smith’s family, and on the second anniversary of Smith’s death, Adams recorded a cover of “Ceremony.” The recordings that followed became Fear Maintenance, a name Adams took from the label that released “I Live,” a 1995 EP by his second Toronto band, In Faith, which played Toronto clubs including Lee’s Palace from 1990 to 1995.

Adams opened the project with a cover of Depeche Mode’s “Stripped” in December 2025, followed by a cover of Joy Division’s “Shadowplay” released with a video on August 13, 2026. “New Dawn Fades” is the third single in the series.

items.title: KOSMOBERKH releases ‘Troglobiten in Absonderlicht’ album
items.summary: Hanover project KOSMOBERKH released "Troglobiten in Absonderlicht" on November 6, 2026, via Zeichenlos Records, its first album since 2018's "oneiroi."
items.fullText:
Hanover, Germany-based project KOSMOBERKH released “Troglobiten in Absonderlicht” on November 6, 2026, via Zeichenlos Records, the label founded by the project’s sole member, David Barteczko. The ten-track album is Barteczko’s first since 2018’s “oneiroi,” released under the project name Mosaikh.

The album’s title translates, in Barteczko’s own rendering, as “Troglobites in Secluded Light.” Acoustic guitar and cello, played by Jann Michael Engel, anchor the record, with synths, electronic percussion and field recordings extending the arrangements beyond their acoustic core. Bandcamp tags the album cinematic, dreamy and experimental, alongside Barteczko’s own term for his work, “singer-doomwriter.” Barteczko names early Dead Can Dance, Scott Walker’s “Scott 4,” David Bowie’s “The Man Who Sold the World” and Peter Hammill’s “In Camera” among his reference points.

Engel’s cello was recorded in Göttingen; Barteczko tracked his own vocals, synths, percussion and effects at home, and most of the guitars were recorded at Holodeck Studio, where Alex Pojda co-produced the album with Barteczko and handled mixing and mastering. Christoffer Grunau plays drums and Udo Kirfel contributes bass on “Telegramme,” and Christof Schlaak plays piano on the closing track, “Petrichor.”

The ten tracks are “Fiz Oblon,” “Asche meiner Jugend,” “Sterngeworden,” “Zugvogel,” “Hybris,” “Telegramme,” “Stummfilm,” “Zypressen,” “Oras Bad” and “Petrichor.” Four advance singles preceded the album: “Stummfilm” (August 14), “Zypressen” (September 4), “Petrichor” (September 25) and “Fiz Oblon” (October 16), each released with its own video.

The black gatefold vinyl edition is limited to 120 copies, and both the LP and the digital download are exclusive to Bandcamp. “Troglobiten in Absonderlicht” is also available on streaming services, including Spotify.

About KOSMOBERKH

KOSMOBERKH is the project of Hanover, Germany-based singer, guitarist and lyricist David Barteczko, who first performed the material on an open stage at Craftwork Café in Oldenburg between 2011 and 2013. The 2014 demo “Urbild” began his recording partnership with Alex Pojda. Barteczko set aside vocals for the instrumental post-rock of “Dim Nachttag” in 2016, then took up singing again on 2018’s “oneiroi,” released under the project name Mosaikh as an electric trio.

During a break from KOSMOBERKH, Barteczko played in the prog-doom band CMDR RIKR and the post-rock group BRUECKEN. He returned to the stage in May 2024, opening for Extra Life at Cadillac in Oldenburg alongside cellist Jann Michael Engel, whose own credits include work with Anne Clark and Mila Mar. “Troglobiten in Absonderlicht” is KOSMOBERKH’s first album since that return, and the first released on Barteczko’s own label, Zeichenlos Records.

items.title: Kontrast – Imperium – Proteus (Digital/Vinyl Album – Danse Macabre Records)
items.summary: The German band Kontrast has been active for some 30 years and boasts an extensive...
items.fullText:
The German band Kontrast has been active for some 30 years and boasts an extensive discography, including a nearly 20-year relationship with Danse Macabre Records. With “Imperium – Proteus”, they complete the two-part album series that began last year with the highly commendable “Imperium – Tyrannis”. Like its predecessor, this album contains 10 tracks. It is also worth noting that both albums are available together as a single CD package.

Upon exploring this release, one immediately notices a distinct difference compared to its predecessor, which, to my ears, sounded harder and was more deeply rooted in an EBM aesthetic. These new tracks lean more towards Electro-Pop, at times even bordering on Future-Pop. Above all, this is an incredibly varied, Pop-oriented record. Its vintage textures occasionally evoke the magic of Welle:Erdball, while other tracks feature harsher arrangements like a wink to Das Ich. The album is primarily danceable, although it also offers a few quieter, more subdued moments. The inclusion of both male and female vocals further enhances the diversity of the overall sound.

Personally, I find the first instalment of the “Imperium” series slightly stronger, but this follow-up certainly has plenty to offer as well. Perhaps the best option is to pick up the CD edition, which brings both releases together in one package. (Rating:7½).

Listen to “Cassettenmensch”:

About Kontrast

The German band Kontrast formed in Germany in 1992, when Dirk Heinrich, Roberto Lindner and Tobias Messias founded the project under the name ISECS; Falko Heinbokel joined in 1995. An early demo of “Einheitsschritt” (“Drei Schritte vor und drei zurück”) appeared in 1994 and grew into an independent-scene anthem by 1996. The band adopted the name Kontrast in 1999, debuting under it that May in support of Clan of Xymox.

Kontrast’s first album, “Programm”, followed in 2002 on the UpSolution label; Danse Macabre Records reissued it as a 20th-anniversary “Programm: Deluxe Edition” in 2022, which reached number two on the Deutsche Alternative Charts and was reviewed by Side-Line. A second album, “Industrie<>Romantik”, appeared in 2004. Kontrast signed to Danse Macabre Records for 2008’s “Vision und Tradition”, which reached the top 10 of the Deutsche Alternative Charts and number one on the German Electronic Web Charts; its single “Durchbruch” also topped the German Electronic Web Charts.

Katrin Möller, performing as Nebelgeist, appeared as a guest vocalist on Kontrast releases before joining full-time. The band’s fourth album, “Balance” (2014), reached number three on the Deutsche Alternative Charts; its single “John Maynard”, a musical setting of Theodor Fontane’s ballad of the same name, reached the top five. A fifth album, “Unaufhaltsam”, followed in 2019 at number four on the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The current line-up is Roberto Lindner (vocals, lyrics), Dirk Heinrich (synthesizers, composition), Falko (synthesizers, mixing) and Nebelgeist (vocals).

Kontrast opened its sixth album as a two-part concept in 2025 with “Imperium – Tyrannis”, exploring a dystopian vision of a dictatorship that transforms people into dance machines. “Imperium – Proteus” completes the project through Danse Macabre Records, with both halves also combined on a single CD alongside separate digital and vinyl editions of each part.

items.title: Hamburg’s Seasurfer Revisits First Love in Video for “Hush Now” — “Trip” EP Out Now!
items.summary: Here we are again You look so familiar In this red light… Drop your mask, my friend Someone you loved at seventeen can say your name across a room and… The post Hamburg’s Seasurfer Revisits First Love in Video for “Hush Now” — “Trip” EP Out Now! appeared first
items.fullText:
Here we are again
You look so familiar
In this red light…
Drop your mask, my friend

Someone you loved at seventeen can say your name across a room and bring back every little thing you did to look at ease. You remember where you put your hands and the joke you made while you worked up the nerve to ask them to stay. The relief came when they heard the question in the joke and stayed a little longer. It can take years to realize how much you miss being known that well.

At the opening of “Hush Now (The Calling),” Apolonia sings to a familiar face bathed in red light, asking them to drop the mask with the gentle insistence of an old friend inviting you to sit and stay awhile. The track is the lead single from Trip, the four-track EP released November 20 by Hamburg noise-pop trio Seasurfer.

Christian Klepp’s footage casts the first verse’s red light across the stage. Red and yellow projections sweep the back wall, while green glints in the dark glasses above a ribbed microphone. Maysterwerke cuts from this intimate close-up to wider shots, where amber haze reduces the band to little more than silhouettes.

Watch the video for Hush Now (The Calling) below.

The way the band moves in and out of view has a counterpart in the arrangements Dirk Knight began imagining in New York. “For me, this is the sound of cities,” says the instrumentalist, who recorded, produced and mixed the EP. He keeps the bass and drums fairly still while the guitars and the voices of Apolonia and Kiora drift in and out of focus.

Those guitars have been a constant since Seasurfer’s first two albums on Saint Marie Records and through collaborations with Cocteau Twins’ Robin Guthrie and producer John Fryer. This year the band put them to work on the post-punk of June’s Angels, then let them fill the room on August’s shoegaze-heavy The Noise is ours. On their third EP of 2026, a trip-hop beat gives the guitar chords more room to ring.

You can hear that space in the first bars of the opening track, One. The guitars drone and the drums take their time, leaving room for the strings that Chandeen’s Harald Löwy adds to the arrangement. The higher voices blur into the chords the way they do on My Bloody Valentine’s Loveless. The low lead comes through with the intimacy of someone speaking in confidence. It’s a seductive way to sing about making peace with your own company and the knowledge that we come and go alone.

 Watch the video for One, filmed by Ahmed Sarowar and edited by Dirk Knight, below:

That intimacy carries into Hush Now (The Calling), where a sigh of synths stretches into long, luminous lines and Knight’s guitars bring warmth up from below. Apolonia and Kiora’s voices cascade through the chorus, opening the melody out the way Elizabeth Fraser could on Cocteau Twins’ Heaven or Las Vegas and Milk & Kisses. Apolonia describes the song as a memory of first love, and Kiora hears loss and longing in the words. When the refrain comes round to “I’m by your side,” the reassurance sounds as necessary to the person giving it as it does to the one hearing it.

The guitar comes further forward on “Disappear”, where the opening loop has the woozy repetition of Cocteau Twins’ Otherness EP. The voice has Cranes’ reserve and some of Portishead’s unease. When the drums drop away, the guitar keeps circling long enough for you to stop anticipating the next hit. By the time it comes, the loop has built up a charge that carries into the closing bars.

The drums make you wait for them again on “I See You”. The guitars pile up first, with the soft-edged distortion of Loveless, and the drum machine gives them a trip-hop lilt when it comes in. There’s some of Cranes’ distance in the singing and some of the poise of Siobhan de Maré on Mono’s “Life in Mono.” At under three minutes, the closer rewards a second pass. Follow a guitar you barely noticed the first time through, and you can hear the arrangement shift around it.

Listen to Trip below and order the EP here.

items.title: BERMUD releases ‘Lost And Anxious’ single
items.summary: Montreal-based electronic shoegaze artist BERMUD released the single and video "Lost And Anxious" on November 20, 2026, ahead of the EP "Incoming Journeys."
items.fullText:
Montreal-based electronic shoegaze artist BERMUD released the single and video “Lost And Anxious” on November 20, 2026. The track is the lead single from the upcoming EP “Incoming Journeys,” due January 15, 2027 via We Are Not Alone Music and L’Autre Distribution, and is the second track on its tracklist.

BERMUD is the solo project of Elliot Aschard, originally from Angers, France, and now based in Montreal, Canada. “Lost And Anxious” pairs the project’s established shoegaze sound with 1990s-style techno beats, a shift from the material on BERMUD’s earlier releases. Aschard commented on the title: “I wanted to express the resilience with which we must face the world. […] We need connection and solidarity to keep from being pulled under by the turmoil. […] I’ve used a shoegaze aesthetic to bring us together, to foster a sense of unity in the face of events over which we have no control.”

About BERMUD

BERMUD is the solo project of Elliot Aschard, a shoegaze artist originally from Angers, France, who relocated to Montreal, Canada, in 2026. “Lost And Anxious” is the lead single from the project’s upcoming EP “Incoming Journeys,” set for release on January 15, 2027 via We Are Not Alone Music and L’Autre Distribution.

items.title: Instinct and Pain announce new album ‘Mauvaises Pensées’
items.summary: Sardinian gothic rock trio Instinct and Pain will release their second album "Mauvaises Pensées" on March 5, 2027 via Morella Records.
items.fullText:
Sardinian gothic rock and darkwave trio Instinct and Pain will release their second album, “Mauvaises Pensées,” on March 5, 2027 via Morella Records. Three singles lead up to the album: “The Death of Love” on December 4, 2026, “Poison Tree (A Garden of Silent Sins)” on January 8, 2027, and “Ashes of Light” on February 26, 2027, when album pre-orders also open on Bandcamp.

The ten-song record takes its title from a collection of thoughts by French poet and writer Paul Valéry, whose ideas inspired most of the songs. The band produced the album themselves, recording it with Salvatore Cabiddu at Tore Cabiddu Studio in Ghilarza and mixing and mastering it with Alberto Bandino at Cut Fire Mix Studio. The closing title track is an instrumental waltz featuring band family members as guests: Ethan Porcu on keyboards, Sara Manca on violin and Giulia Loi on clarinet.

“We would like people to hear our voice, what we feel through music, and the passion and commitment we put into making these songs,” said Alessandro Manca of Instinct and Pain.

Blake Carpenter, founder of Morella Records, described the band’s growth: “Instinct and Pain is a three-year-old band that sounds like they’ve been together for decades. The music is riveting, pure gothic post-punk, the vocals are brilliant and the musicianship is top notch. I’m honored to call Instinct and Pain a Morella family member.”

Tracklist

  1. Poison Tree (A Garden Of Silent Sins)
  2. The Death Of Love
  3. The Storm
  4. Ashes of Light
  5. Dust Claims All
  6. Over and Over
  7. Hope On a Tightrope
  8. Happiness With Closed Eyes
  9. I’m Nothing
  10. Mauvaises Pensées (instrumental)

Release schedule

  • January 8, 2027: “Poison Tree (A Garden of Silent Sins)”
  • February 26, 2027: “Ashes of Light,” album pre-orders open on Bandcamp
  • March 5, 2027: “Mauvaises Pensées” album, on Bandcamp and streaming platforms

About Instinct and Pain

Instinct and Pain is a gothic rock and darkwave trio from Ghilarza, Sardinia, Italy, formed in 2023 by Alessandro Manca (vocals, guitar), Luca Porcu (bass) and Nicola Loi (drums). The band builds its songs on dark atmosphere and melancholic melody, with post-punk bones and a debt to the darker side of the 1980s underground.

Its debut album, “All Is Gone,” drew attention from the Italian press; critic Mick Mercer described the band as “vibrant Sardinian goth.” “Mauvaises Pensées,” the band’s second album, follows via Morella Records on March 5, 2027.

items.title: Night Nail releases ‘Feelings Are Monsters’ single and video
items.summary: Berlin darkwave act Night Nail released the single and video "Feelings Are Monsters" on November 20, 2026, the third single from "Infinite Fountain."
items.fullText:
Berlin darkwave act Night Nail released the single and video “Feelings Are Monsters” on November 20, 2026. The track is the third single from the band’s upcoming album “Infinite Fountain,” and is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

Night Nail is the project of frontman Brandon Robert, who splits his creative base between Berlin and Los Angeles. Before starting the project, Robert worked as a hired-hand bassist in Hollywood. He has described a breaking point with a former bandmate who told him to “cheer up” during a period of depression: “I decided that day to never play for someone else’s dream again. I started recording my own music. I learned the hard way that no one tells your story for you.”

Recommend to fans of Echo & the Bunnymen, The Cure and Clock DVA.

About Night Nail

Night Nail is a darkwave project founded by Brandon Robert around 2014, splitting its base between Berlin and Los Angeles. The band marked 10 years of its earliest recordings in July 2024 with “Early Demons & Demos 10th Anniversary Edition”.

The project first drew Side-Line’s attention in September 2023 with “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher”, the first single from an album released via Metropolis Records. “Fates Explained” followed as a video single that November, and in January 2024 the band released “Cracks In My Heart”, a video single featuring Luna De La Torre on vocals.

Night Nail’s sound draws on influences including Echo & the Bunnymen, The Comsat Angels, Trisomie 21, The Cult, The Sound, Christian Death, Wire, The Contortions, Clock DVA and The Cure. “Feelings Are Monsters” is the third single from the band’s upcoming album “Infinite Fountain.”

items.title: Conn.RAR releases EBM single ‘You Don’t Care’
items.summary: Conn.RAR has released the EBM single "You Don't Care" on Bandcamp and Spotify, written by founder Connor Eck after a corporate layoff.
items.fullText:
EBM act Conn.RAR released the single “You Don’t Care” on 20 November 2026, available on Bandcamp and Spotify.

The song addresses executive greed and the treatment of laid-off workers. Conn.RAR founder Connor Eck says the subject is a personal one: “We, the employees of the company I’d been working for were all educated, talented and had experience. But, despite all of that, we all got laid off when my employer was bought out.” Eck wrote, produced, mixed and mastered the track himself.

“You Don’t Care” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify.

About Conn.RAR

Conn.RAR is the solo project of Connor Eck, who started out in 2020 making electronic music inspired by old video games and cyberpunk themes before shifting toward the hard, punchy EBM sound of acts like Front 242, A Split-Second and a;GRUMH. “You Don’t Care” is Conn.RAR’s latest single, built around Eck’s own experience of a corporate layoff.

items.title: Pawn Pawn releases synthpop single ‘Silhouette’
items.summary: Pawn Pawn has released the synthpop single "Silhouette," the first taste of the Toledo, Ohio trio's upcoming album "Thunder," due in early 2027.
items.fullText:
Synthpop trio Pawn Pawn released the single “Silhouette” on 20 November 2026, the first taste of the Toledo, Ohio band’s upcoming album “Thunder,” due in early 2027.

“Silhouette” pairs driving guitars with synth bass over a programmed beat. Lyrically, the song addresses the gap between a person’s unfiltered self and the version expected to be shown in public, where vulnerability is the price of being fully seen.

Liz Owens Boltz handles lead and backing vocals and wrote the lyrics. David Daniel Smith plays percussion and keys and adds backing vocals, while Brandon William Boltz plays guitar and backing vocals. The track was recorded by Brandon W. Boltz and David D. Smith at NoFocus Records and produced by the band, with mixing and mastering by Brett Dennison at FireFly Studios. Cover art is by CatBot Industries.

“Silhouette” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify.

About Pawn Pawn

Pawn Pawn is a synthpop trio from Toledo, Ohio, combining rhythmic energy and dark soundscapes with subtle industrial-pop elements. The band has played live original music in Northwest Ohio since 2018 and headlined the Toledo Pride Kick-off Party in 2026. Side-Line previously streamed the band’s “Halloween” EP exclusively ahead of its release in January 2025. “Silhouette” is the band’s latest single and the first song revealed from “Thunder,” the album Pawn Pawn has set for an early 2027 release.

About Laibach

Laibach formed in 1980 in Trbovlje, Slovenia, taking its name from the German name for Ljubljana under Habsburg and Nazi occupation. The group became the musical wing of the Neue Slowenische Kunst art collective, built around a confrontational aesthetic that reworks totalitarian imagery, military iconography and mass-culture symbols into statements whose political meaning stays ambiguous. Laibach signed to Mute in the UK during the 1980s and built a catalogue of reinterpretations alongside original material, including the 1987 album “Opus Dei” and its cover of Queen’s “One Vision”.

Across more than four decades, Laibach has continued to reinterpret other artists’ work as a core part of its method, from “Wat” (2003) through recent singles covering Foreigner’s “I Want To Know What Love Is”, Billie Holiday’s “Strange Fruit” and a tribute album of Rammstein covers. The band’s live work has ranged from a 2015 concert in Pyongyang, North Korea, to the large-scale symphonic project “Alamut” with A/Political in 2025.

In 2026, Laibach moved toward a more direct pop sound on the album “MUSICK”, built around high-concept electropop production and features from pop, electronic and underground guests across several countries. “MUSICK : ENCORE” extends that album with its outtakes and remixes, alongside the band’s continuing European tour dates into 2027.

items.title: Then Comes Silence split ‘Requiem Ballroom’ into two halves for eighth album
items.summary: Then Comes Silence release eighth album "Requiem Ballroom" on Metropolis Records, led by focus track "Witches and Demons", ahead of a January 2027 EU tour.
items.fullText:
Stockholm post-punk trio Then Comes Silence release their eighth album, ‘Requiem Ballroom’, on Metropolis Records, led by focus track ‘Witches and Demons’. Side-Line reported the album’s announcement in October; the 12-track album splits into two six-track halves, “Requiem” and “Ballroom,” each mixed separately around a theme of polarity.

Jon Bordon (Nicole Sabouné, Melody Club, The Exploding Boy) mixed the “Ballroom” half and Tom van Heesch (Rammstein, Apocalyptica, Backyard Babies) mixed the “Requiem” half. Svante Forsbäck handled mastering. Vocalist-bassist Alex Svenson produced the album and wrote all the lyrics and music. Drummer Jonas Fransson and guitarist Hugo Zombie complete the trio. Agent Side Grinder‘s Johan Lange adds synthesizer on the closing track.

“Since the album is divided into two halves, it’s important to give each part its own sound. It carries its own identity and the context is somewhat varied. That’s why we have two mixing producers, Tom van Heesch and Jon Bordon, each of whom takes care of one half. This album is simultaneously a game, a social experiment playing with polarisation. You pick one team. You can’t have both sides. Choose Requiem or Ballroom,” says Alex Svenson.

‘Requiem Ballroom’ follows the singles ‘Judgement Day’, ‘Remaker Redeemer’ and ‘Bye Bye Land’, released ahead of the album.

About Then Comes Silence

Then Comes Silence was formed in Stockholm in 2012 by vocalist-bassist Alex Svenson. Drummer Jonas Fransson and guitarist Hugo Zombie complete the band’s current line-up. “Aggressor” is sung entirely in German and was produced, arranged and mixed by frontman Steve Naghavi. “Krieger” was the album’s only single and remains a fan favourite, alongside “Schwarz” and “Fernsehapparat.” Across twelve tracks, the album pairs the band’s EBM roots with its synthpop hooks.

Some Days Are Darker began as the solitary songwriting project of former metalcore guitarist Lear Mason before growing into a three-piece with bassist, guitarist and keyboardist Chris Martin and drummer, multi-instrumentalist and producer Robbie Williamson. The band is based in New York.

items.title: Test Dept and Brith Gof share ‘Truan Yw Gennyf Fi / Lament’ single
items.summary: Test Dept and Brith Gof release 'Truan Yw Gennyf Fi / Lament', the third single from 'Gododdin: 2026 Remaster', out 4 December via Artoffact Records.
items.fullText:
London industrial group Test Dept and Welsh theatre company Brith Gof released the single “Truan Yw Gennyf Fi / Lament (Live in Polverigi 1989, 2026 Remaster)” on 20 November 2026 via Artoffact Records. It is the third advance single from “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster,” a 3CD/1DVD box set expanding the pair’s 1989 album “Gododdin,” due 4 December 2026.

The single is accompanied by a video assembled from footage of a 1989 live performance in a quarry in Polverigi, Italy, with the audio of the full show appearing on the third disc of the reissue. It follows two earlier advance singles from the same campaign: “Gwr A Aeth Gatraeth / Prologue (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026)” and “Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026)”.

“We were physical performers as well as musicians in the live show, and in the aftermath of the battle we lay prostrate, exhausted in the mud of the flooded quarry as the bagpipes struck up heralding the lament for the fallen warriors,” says Test Dept’s Paul Jamrozy. “I had actually been a split second away from being a real fatality myself when a burning battering ram log broke free, hurtling down and crashing into the huge metal tank beside my head.”

“It was thrilling to be a part of this event, singing the ancient words of the poet Aneirin to music by Test Dept and John E R Hardy,” adds Brith Gof’s Lis Hughes Jones. “I looked out over the vast expanse of the sand quarry where a stunned audience stood as witnesses to the aftermath of battle. As the song came to an end the mournful sound of bagpipes took up the lament for the fallen.”

“Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” widens the original seven-track album with 19 previously unreleased recordings, for a total of 26 tracks across three CDs. The set includes a reworked perspective on the original release, drawn from multitrack tapes of early studio recordings, alongside the third disc capturing the 1989 Polverigi performance in full. A DVD carries a contemporaneous documentary combining live footage with interviews. All audio was remastered by Paul Lavigne at Kontrast Mastering. The reissue is packaged in a 5-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet containing archival imagery and an essay by author Alexei Monroe. A separate red vinyl LP carries the original album with one previously unreleased track. Artwork for both formats comes from Paul Jamrozy and Stefan Alt (ant-zen).

The original “Gododdin” was produced by Ken Thomas at Jacobs Studios, built from Test Dept’s existing studio and field recordings augmented with brass and wind courtesy of Brith Gof’s John E R Hardy and bagpipes from Alistair Adams, with Jamrozy’s vocals set alongside Welsh-language vocals from Lis Hughes Jones. The piece is based on Y Gododdin, the earliest surviving Welsh-language poem, written around 600 AD, which tells of 300 Celtic warriors who attacked 100,000 invading Angles and lost. Test Dept and Brith Gof first staged it live at an abandoned Rover car factory in Cardiff in December 1988, with further performances in 1989 in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” is the second entry in a series of Test Dept archival reissues, following the 4xCD “Industrial Overture. Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985” roughly a year earlier.

Test Dept have the following live shows confirmed:

  • 28 November 2026, Porto, Portugal, Auditório CCOP
  • 1-4 July 2027, Canterbury, UK, Shadowlands Festival

About Test Dept and Brith Gof

Test Dept formed in London in the early 1980s around Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy, building an industrial sound from scrap metal percussion, factory tools and found objects alongside electronics, aligned with the miners’ strikes and labour politics of the era. Brith Gof is a Welsh avant-garde theatre company co-founded by Mike Pearson, known for large-scale, site-specific performance work staged in disused industrial buildings and open landscapes across Wales.

The two groups collaborated on “Gododdin,” a studio album and accompanying performance piece centered on the Welsh poem Y Gododdin, first staged at a derelict car factory in Cardiff in December 1988 with Lis Hughes Jones and John E R Hardy of Brith Gof joining Test Dept on stage. The production toured Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland through 1989, including the Polverigi quarry performance captured on the current reissue’s third disc.

Test Dept signed to Artoffact Records in 2025 for a series of catalogue reissues and new material, beginning with the 4xCD “Industrial Overture. Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985”. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” follows as the second release in that campaign, preceded by advance singles “Gwr A Aeth Gatraeth / Prologue” and “Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society,” with the full 3CD/1DVD box set due 4 December 2026.

items.title: Projekt Ich’s ‘The Night Before Christmas’ single out now via Echozone
items.summary: Projekt Ich's new synth-pop Christmas single "The Night Before Christmas" is out now via Echozone, featuring Suzanne Letting and Manfred Thomaser.
items.fullText:
German synth-pop project Projekt Ich released “The Night Before Christmas” on 20 November 2026 through Echozone, pairing a Christmas Eve mood with themes of peace and hope for future generations.

The lyrics were written by Suzanne Letting, who previously provided vocals for the title track of Projekt Ich’s album “A Beautiful Day In Autumn,” continuing her collaboration with Ulf Müller. Manfred Thomaser, who together with Müller forms the dark electro duo The Grab Society, contributes backing vocals; Thomaser also records with Arsine Tibé, Demokratie and The Independent Seasons. The track was mastered by Bernd Abromeit at Tonschleifer.

The single is released as a download, alongside an instrumental version. Projekt Ich plans an animated, AI-assisted music video for the song, set to premiere on the band’s YouTube channel in early December.

About Projekt Ich

Projekt Ich is a German synth-pop and electronic project led by Ulf Müller, built around recurring collaborations with guest vocalists. The project’s catalogue includes the album “A Beautiful Day In Autumn,” featuring Suzanne Letting on the title track, and a string of singles released through Echozone featuring artists such as Stian Shiver, Frecuencias Ocultas and Alex Braun.

Side-Line previously covered the project’s single “In The Fire,” feat. Stian Shiver, released in March 2026, and the 2021 single “Mit dir,” which featured 20 remixes.

“The Night Before Christmas” continues that collaborative pattern, reuniting Müller with Suzanne Letting and adding Manfred Thomaser’s backing vocals for a seasonal release timed to the start of Advent.

items.title: CØLDSTAR’s ‘Into The Void’ sends an astronaut into deep space

items.fullText:
Swiss electronic duo CØLDSTAR released a new single, “Into The Void,” on 20 November 2026 through Town & Towers Records.

The song follows an astronaut 300 miles above Earth, watching a planet lit by millions of screens where people stay connected without finding real connection. Driven by a pulsating electronic rhythm, the track presents the darkness of space as a place of freedom and clarity, echoed in its refrain: “Into the void, it’s not empty at all.”

About CØLDSTAR

Based in Bern, Switzerland, CØLDSTAR is the duo of Martin Baumann and Michael Freund, working across darkwave and synthpop, with lyrics exploring isolation and technology.

Following an early 2021 interpretation of Nine Inch Nails’ “Hurt,” CØLDSTAR established its own musical direction with the “Coming Home” EP in 2023, followed by debut album “CØSMIC DUST” in 2024.

“Into The Void” follows a string of CØLDSTAR singles that includes “Last Night On Earth,” “Time Machine,” “Astronaut’s Lament” and “Last Dance,” all released through Town & Towers Records.

items.title: Depeche Mode announce ‘Memento Mori: The 12-Inch Singles’ box set for January 2027
items.summary: Depeche Mode will release "Memento Mori: The 12-Inch Singles," a seven-disc vinyl box set of remixes and new sessions, on January 29, 2027, via Sony Music.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode will release “Memento Mori: The 12-Inch Singles,” a seven-disc vinyl box set collecting remixes and new recordings tied to the band’s 15th studio album, on January 29, 2027, according to depechemode.de. Sony Music is issuing the set in a deluxe numbered slipcase, continuing the label’s ongoing “12-Inch Singles” box series covering the band’s catalog.

Six of the seven discs gather official remixes of “Memento Mori”‘s five singles. “Ghosts Again” fills the first disc alone, with eight remixes including versions by Chris Liebing vs. Luke Slater, Miss Grit and Rival Consoles. “Wagging Tongue” spans two discs of remixes, by artists including Richie Hawtin, Daniel Avery and Gabe Gurnsey, and that second disc also carries remixes of “My Cosmos Is Mine” and “Speak To Me.” “My Favourite Stranger,” “Before We Drown” and “People Are Good” each fill a further disc, with remixers including Boris Brejcha, Ela Minus, Chris Avantgarde and Indira Paganotto.

The seventh disc is the set’s new material. Side A, “The Memento Mori Sessions,” holds four additional studio recordings: “Survive,” “Life 2.0,” “Give Yourself To Me” and “In The End.” Side B, “The Vinegar Hill Sessions,” is the first physical release of stripped-back performances of “Ghosts Again,” “Wagging Tongue” and “My Favourite Stranger,” recorded live at Vinegar Hill Sound in New York in 2022.

“Ghosts Again,” the original lead single from “Memento Mori,” arrived with this Anton Corbijn-directed video in February 2023, one of the tracks now collected across the new box set’s first disc. Side-Line covered the single’s original announcement ahead of the album’s release.

About Depeche Mode

Depeche Mode formed in Basildon, England, in 1980, with founding members Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Andy Fletcher and Dave Gahan. The band signed to Mute Records and released its debut album, “Speak & Spell,” in 1981; Clarke left the band the same year to form Yazoo and later Erasure, and Gore took over as primary songwriter. Alan Wilder joined in 1982 and remained until 1995. Through the 1980s and 1990s the band built its catalog with albums including “Construction Time Again,” “Some Great Reward,” “Black Celebration,” “Music For The Masses,” “Violator” and “Songs Of Faith And Devotion,” moving from early synth-pop into the darker electronic and industrial-tinged sound that defined its mid-career work.

Fletcher died in May 2022. “Memento Mori,” the band’s 15th studio album and its first after Fletcher’s death, was produced by James Ford with additional production by Marta Salogni and released on March 24, 2023, led by the single “Ghosts Again.” The band, now the duo of Gahan and Gore, toured the album through 2023 and 2024 and later released the concert film “Depeche Mode: M” and the live album “Memento Mori: Mexico City.”

“Memento Mori: The 12-Inch Singles,” the catalog box set collecting the album’s singles and new session recordings, is due January 29, 2027 via Sony Music.

items.title: Still Ruins share video for ‘Armor Of Mourning’, from debut album ‘Through The Glass’
items.summary: Still Ruins share a video for "Armor Of Mourning," the closing track on debut album "Through The Glass," due February 26, 2027 on Born Losers Records.
items.fullText:
Oakland, California post-punk quartet Still Ruins has released a video for “Armor Of Mourning,” the closing track on its debut album, “Through The Glass,” due February 26, 2027 on Born Losers Records.

“Through The Glass” is a ten-track album pressed on sea-blue vinyl, with CD, cassette and digital editions also listed on the label’s Bandcamp page. The record was mixed by Kurt Feldman of Ice Choir and The Pains Of Being Pure At Heart, who also contributed additional sequencing and backing vocals. It was recorded at bandmate Jose Medina’s home studio. Claire Wardlaw plays saxophone on the opening track, “Permanence.” The cover artwork is by Mario Luna.

The video for “Armor Of Mourning” was shot and edited by Eli Wengrin. Of the song’s place as the album’s closer, the band said: “As soon as we finished writing this song we knew it was going to be the final track on the record.”

“Through The Glass” follows a self-titled EP the band released on the Oakland label Smoking Room.

About Still Ruins

Still Ruins is a post-punk quartet from Oakland, California. The band’s own Bandcamp artist page dates its founding to 2020, while the “Through The Glass” album notes describe vocalist Frankie Soto and multi-instrumentalist Jose Medina as having “began Still Ruins” in 2018, writing and recording together at Medina’s home studio before the project grew into a full band. Bassist Cyrus VandenBerghe joined to help turn the home-recording project into a live act, and keyboardist Marcos Gonzalez completed the current lineup in 2025.

Before forming Still Ruins, the members spent years in the Central Valley DIY scene. The band released a self-titled EP on the Oakland label Smoking Room and has shared bills with Provoker, House Of Harm and Johnny Dynamite.

Still Ruins’ debut album, “Through The Glass,” is due February 26, 2027 on Born Losers Records, led by the video for “Armor Of Mourning.”

The four-track EP covers a wide range of the project’s sound, moving from brooding atmospheres to noise-driven industrial rhythms and synths. Silent Impulse describes the release as both a reflection of the ground covered on its previous releases and a glimpse of where the project is heading next.

Across a steadily growing catalogue of releases, Silent Impulse has worked at the contrast between aggression and atmosphere, mechanical precision and organic instability, dissonance and melody, balancing physical intensity with a darker, introspective undercurrent. “Transmutation” is the project’s newest release, out 20 November 2026.
